I will keep my full 4.1 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is the system I know best and it fits my land, my well irrigation, and the labor my family can still put in. I farm on a small area, and at my age I want a plan that is steady, familiar, and not too risky. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put on enough fertilizer to keep the stand strong, irrigate a few key times, and manage weeds and disease with a limited number of sprays. After wheat harvest, I will put the same land straight into summer maize. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want stable ears and better yield, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate when the crop most needs it, and control pests with a small number of applications. I will use rotary tillage because it is practical on my small farm and works well for this rotation. I am not trying to chase the highest possible yield; I am trying to get a dependable harvest with work and costs that my household can manage.
